# Canonical Skills — Deep Context

## Purpose
This module is the repo's prompt-programming core. The markdown skill files under `plugins/edc/skills/` define how build, update, split, audit, and differential review should behave across all supported agent runtimes.

## Files In Scope
- `plugins/edc/skills/edc-build-impl/SKILL.md`
- `plugins/edc/skills/edc-update-impl/SKILL.md`
- `plugins/edc/skills/edc-split-impl/SKILL.md`
- `plugins/edc/skills/edc-audit-impl/SKILL.md`
- `plugins/edc/skills/edc-context/**`
- `plugins/edc/skills/edc-review-impl/**`

## Core Responsibilities
- Define when to do a full build vs incremental update.
- Define the shape of `.context/context.md`, `.context/{module}.md`, `.context/issues.md`, `.context/.meta.json`, and `.context/complexity.md`.
- Define the deep-analysis methodology (`edc-context`) that upstream build/update flows rely on.
- Define the structured differential-review methodology and reporting format used by the orchestrator.
- Provide prompt material that benchmark/autoresearch can mutate and score.

## Internal Relationships
- `edc-build-impl` is the top-level router and post-build instruction-file updater.
- `edc-update-impl` assumes `.context/full-context.md` and `.context/.meta.json` already exist.
- `edc-split-impl` converts monolithic analysis into overview/modules/issues/meta without dropping content.
- `edc-audit-impl` compares code size/shape against the context model.
- `edc-context` is intentionally pure context-building only.
- `edc-review-impl` is decomposed into methodology/adversarial/pattern/reporting support files to enable independent tuning.

## Invariants and Assumptions
- Skill directory names are part of the runtime API; shell wrappers search for exact names.
- Full-context analysis must be rich enough to split losslessly into module files.
- Complexity audit is downstream of context generation, not a substitute for it.
- Review methodology files are both user-visible prompt content and benchmark mutation targets.

## Trust Boundaries
- The shell/runtime layer treats these markdown files as executable instructions for agent subprocesses.
- Benchmark tooling intentionally mutates review prompt files and evaluates them empirically.

## Cross-Module Coupling
- Used directly by `scripts/edc`, `scripts/edc-review.sh`, Cursor/Codex wrappers, and benchmark/autoresearch scripts.
- Hardening tests depend on the routing conventions these files encode.

## Issues and Fragility
- Large prompt surfaces create a high drift risk between runtime docs, tests, and expected behavior.
- Dirty edits to prompt files directly affect benchmark behavior and can change review quality without touching shell code.
